_comment: The second and third paragraphs of an expanded card.
The compact card carries one assembled paragraph. Opening it should be
worth the tap, so the expansion adds two more, and they are assembled
the same way everything else here is: from tables keyed off the parts of
the measurement, never written per day and never written per person.
area     what this means for that part of a life   9 x 5 tones
natal    what that part of you is                  12, angles included
tone     what that kind of angle does               5
transit  how long it lasts, and why                10
── Why `area` exists, and what went wrong without it ──
The first version had no area dimension. Paragraph two was natal plus
tone and paragraph three was transit, which meant that expanding the
Love card and expanding the Work card produced the *same two paragraphs*
whenever the two aspects happened to share a body. Nine cards, and the
insides of them converged. It read as a template because it was one.
So the expansion now goes specific, specific, mechanical:
1  the reading            what today is
2  area x tone            what that means for this part of a life
3  natal + tone + transit which two points, what angle, how long
Paragraph three is allowed to sound like an explanation because it is
one, and it is labelled as one by sitting last, under two that are not.
9 x 5 areas, times 12 naturals, times 10 transits, is 5,400 distinct
three-paragraph expansions from 72 written pieces. That ratio is the
whole method, and the reason it is honest is that the address is printed
underneath: the reader sees which two bodies, which angle and how many
degrees, and can check that the paragraph they were given is the one
that address selects.
No proper nouns. Not one of these names a planet, because the card prints
the planet from the chart and a line that named it could be wrong. The
same rule governs readings.json, touches.json and signs.json.

natal.sun: This is the part of you that wants to be recognised as itself. When something lands on it, the day turns on being seen accurately, and being seen wrongly costs more than it usually would.
natal.moon: This is the part that reacts before you have decided anything. It sets the weather of a day several minutes ahead of your reasoning, which is why the mood arrives first and the explanation second.
natal.mercury: This is how you sort, name and hand things over. An angle here shows up in the wording of a message, the order of a list, the sentence you rewrite four times before sending.
natal.venus: This is what you are drawn towards, and what you are willing to pay for it. It governs taste, affection, and the quiet arithmetic of what a thing is worth to you.
natal.mars: This is the part that starts things, and the part that argues. It is your appetite for friction, and an angle here tends to arrive as impatience well before it arrives as a decision.
natal.jupiter: This is where you overreach in the useful direction. It widens whatever it touches, mistakes included, which is why a contact here feels generous and needs a limit put on it from outside.
natal.saturn: This is the part that has already counted the cost. It slows things down on purpose, and what it asks for is not effort so much as time served.
natal.uranus: This is the part of you that will not be settled on anyone else's schedule. It works by interruption, which is useful about as often as it is inconvenient, and a contact here tends to arrive as a sudden unwillingness to carry on exactly as before.
natal.neptune: This is where your outline is softest. It is the part that imagines, forgives and occasionally fails to notice what it is being asked to give away, and an angle here is felt long before it can be described.
natal.pluto: This is the part of you that does not do things by halves and does not explain itself. It holds on hard, it goes further down than is comfortable, and what it touches is changed rather than adjusted.
natal.ascendant: This is not a planet. It is the degree of the sky that was climbing over the horizon at the minute you were born, which is why it fixes the whole sector layout, and why an angle to it shows up in how you land on a room before it shows up in anything you do.
natal.midheaven: This is not a planet either. It is the degree that was directly overhead when you were born, the highest point the sky reached, and it stands for the part of a life other people can see from a distance: the standing, the reputation, the answer to what it is you do.

tone.charged: Two bodies in the same degree do not pull in a direction. They amplify, and what they amplify is whatever was already running. That is why this angle is the hardest one to give advice about and the easiest one to notice.
tone.open: This angle is an opening rather than a push. Nothing here forces itself on the day; it is available, and it stays available only while the angle holds.
tone.friction: This angle is ninety degrees of disagreement between two parts of a chart that both want the day. It does not resolve by picking a winner. It resolves by doing the smaller, duller thing that neither part objects to.
tone.easy: This angle costs nothing, which is exactly its risk. What runs clean tends to run unattended, and the day can pass without the ease having been spent on anything.
tone.pull: This angle puts two parts of your chart at opposite ends of one line. Both are real and both are yours. The work is not picking one, it is admitting the trade rather than pretending there is not one.

transit.moon: The body making this angle covers thirteen degrees a day, so the contact forms and breaks inside a few hours. Whatever it is doing, it is not doing it tomorrow.
transit.sun: The body making this angle moves about a degree a day, so this is a matter of days rather than of hours. It comes to exact, holds briefly, and is gone inside the week.
transit.mercury: The body making this angle is quick, and it turns retrograde three times a year, so a contact from it can arrive, leave, and arrive again inside a couple of months.
transit.venus: The body making this angle takes a few days over it. Long enough to be a mood rather than a moment, short enough that waiting it out is a real option.
transit.mars: The body making this angle holds it for the better part of a week. That is long enough to make a decision under and long enough to regret one, which is the argument for deciding late rather than early.
transit.jupiter: The body making this angle moves about a degree a month, so this is a season and not a day. What it opens stays open for weeks.
transit.saturn: The body making this angle moves a few minutes of arc a day, so the contact has been forming for weeks and will take weeks to let go. Nothing about it is urgent and nothing about it is optional.
transit.uranus: The body making this angle takes about seven years to cross a sector, so a contact from it is a year of a life rather than a day of one. What it dislodges does not go back.
transit.neptune: The body making this angle moves a couple of degrees a year, so this has been forming for months and will take months to clear. Nothing about it is sudden and nothing about it is precise.
transit.pluto: The body making this angle covers about two arcseconds a day, so this contact spans seasons and can return two or three times before it is finished. It is the slowest thing on this page by a wide margin.

self.charged: This lands on how you arrive rather than on what you do, which is why it will be noticed before it is understood. People will read something off you today that you did not decide to put there.
self.open: Being seen accurately is easier today than it usually is. That is worth spending on something specific rather than letting it pass as a good mood.
self.friction: The gap today is between how you land and how you meant to land. Nobody else is measuring that gap, which is the useful thing to remember about it.
self.easy: You are legible today. The version of you that arrives in a room and the version you would describe are close enough together to stop managing the difference.
self.pull: Who you are and what is being asked of you are at opposite ends of one line today. Both are real, and the honest move is to name which end you are standing at.

money.charged: This lands on what you are worth and what you will trade time for, which are two questions that get confused under pressure. Today they are loud enough to separate.
money.open: A number is easier to say out loud today. The gap between what you charge and what you would quote somebody else is a habit, and habits move on days like this.
money.friction: The strain is in the arithmetic you have been avoiding doing. Not the amount, the arithmetic, and the two feel identical until one of them is written down.
money.easy: Effort converts today at a better rate than usual. That makes it a day for the thing you have been undercharging for rather than the thing that is easy to invoice.
money.pull: Two prices are pulling against each other and only one of them can be paid. What it costs elsewhere is the part that is easy to leave out of the sum.

talk.charged: This lands on how the talking goes, so a sentence carries further today than you intend it to. Send the direct version; the softened one will be the one misread.
talk.open: Conversation is cheap today and it compounds. An introduction between two people costs nothing now and is worth something in a year.
talk.friction: What you are saying and what is being heard are not the same today. The short reply is the accurate one, and explaining twice makes it worse.
talk.easy: The long conversation goes well today. It will be shorter and warmer than the rehearsal in your head led you to expect.
talk.pull: You are being pulled between the people you talk to and the ones you actually run with, and today those are not the same set.

home.charged: This lands where you are from and where you sleep, so it arrives privately and probably before you are dressed. It is not asking politely.
home.open: One small thing at home is worth doing today. Just the one. The instinct to make it a project is what turns a good day into a lost weekend.
home.friction: Something at home is resisting, and the temptation is to answer it by improving the room. The room is not the question.
home.easy: The house is on your side today, which you only notice by using it. Cook for somebody in it.
home.pull: Where you came from and where you live now are pulling in different directions today, and neither of them is wrong to.

making.charged: This lands on what you make, so the work is louder than usual and less patient. Start badly on purpose; the good version is downstream of a bad one existing.
making.open: The idea is available today at a price it will not be at next week. Take the rough version and stop improving it.
making.friction: The work resists today. That is a fact about the work and not about you, and the answer to it is the unglamorous half rather than a better mood.
making.easy: It comes out clean today. Point that at the thing that has been stuck rather than at the thing that was already going to be fine.
making.pull: Making it and showing it want opposite hours today. One of them is the work and the other is the account of the work.

work.charged: This lands on the daily work and on what it is building you a name for, and those two are not the same thing. Today they are close enough together to notice the difference.
work.open: There is room above your level today and it is open rather than offered. Asking is the whole mechanism; nothing here arrives unasked.
work.friction: The wall at work is real today. Testing it again is the expensive option and going around it is the cheap one.
work.easy: Effort converts today, which makes it the day for the stuck thing rather than the easy one. Ease spent on what was already fine is ease wasted.
work.pull: What you are doing and what you are known for are pulling apart. One of them pays and one of them matters, and today they want opposite hours.

love.charged: This lands on the other person, so it is not a private matter today however much you would prefer it to be. The direct sentence is the one that lands.
love.open: The difficult conversation goes better today than it will tomorrow. That is the whole of the opportunity, and it does not stay open.
love.friction: You are not going to win this one today. Try not needing to; the version of this that resolves is the one where nobody is keeping score.
love.easy: Warmth is cheap today. Spend it on the person rather than on the arrangement, which is where it tends to get spent instead.
love.pull: What you want and what they want are at opposite ends of one line. Both ends are reasonable, which is exactly what makes it hard to admit the trade.

sex.charged: This lands on closeness and on what you take pleasure in, which is the part of a life most felt and least said out loud. It is close to the surface today.
sex.open: Saying the plain thing about what you want is easier today than it usually is, and it is likelier to be met well than you are assuming.
sex.friction: The strain is in the grip rather than in the thing being gripped. Withholding is a decision too, and today it is the expensive one.
sex.easy: You can be close today without it costing what closeness usually costs. That is rarer than it sounds and it does not last the week.
sex.pull: What you want and what you are willing to ask for are the two ends of this. Naming which is which is most of the work.

belief.charged: This lands on what you hold true and on the far-off, so it arrives as a question about the shape of things rather than about today. It will not be settled today either.
belief.open: The distant thing is closer today. Look at it properly rather than deciding about it, which is the mistake this day invites.
belief.friction: The big argument is not the one to have today. There is a small true one underneath it and that one is winnable.
belief.easy: The generous reading is also the accurate one today, which is not always the case and is worth using while it is.
belief.pull: What you hold true and what you can show are pulling apart. That gap is uncomfortable and it is also the only honest place to stand in it.
